h1:
Bang Pakong Riverside Cafes
+ Walking Paet Riu Old Town
intro: Chachoengsao sits just over an hour from Bangkok, but the pace drops the moment you arrive. The Bang Pakong River runs through the middle of town, there's a century-old wooden market, and new riverside cafes keep opening every year. We put together a 2-day, 1-night plan made for coffee lovers: starting with riverside cafes, walking the old town, then wrapping up at the 100-year-old Ban Mai Market. Every spot here is still open, and we checked the hours for you.

blocks.html: Paet Riu (the local name for Chachoengsao town) is great for a slow weekend trip. The draw is the cluster of cafes along the Bang Pakong River, spread across both the town center and the Ban Mai Market area, plus an old town where you can pay respects at temples, look at old Chinese shophouses, and find good food all within a short walk. This plan keeps day one focused on cafes and walking, then catches the century-old market on the second morning before heading home. Feel free to swap the order depending on which days you visit.

blocks.title: Read this before picking your dates
blocks.html: The 100-year-old Ban Mai Market is only open Saturday–Sunday and public holidays, 8:00 AM–5:00 PM. If you want to catch the market, plan your trip across a Saturday or Sunday. The in-town cafes are open every day.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Riverside cafes + old town walk

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Leave Bangkok mid-morning, arrive in Paet Riu before noon

items.activity: Arrive in Chachoengsao, check in at a hotel in town
items.note: From Bangkok it's about 1–1.5 hours via the motorway or the Bang Na–Trat road. You can also take the Eastern Line train and get off at Chachoengsao station.

items.activity: Start with a late breakfast at Nava House Cafe on the Bang Pakong River
items.note: This cafe shares the grounds with Pukae Riverside restaurant. There's an air-conditioned room right by the water and a shaded outdoor zone under the trees. Drinks start around 70–110 THB.

items.activity: Head into the old town and stop at Tang Seng Chua Saen Phudat
items.note: This is the big new branch of Tang Seng Chua, a mooncake-pastry brand with over 90 years of history. The building is done up in a Korean-palace style and has become a photo landmark. There's a cafe, pastries, and souvenirs to choose from. Drinks around 45–70 THB.

items.activity: Walk Paet Riu old town, looking at the wooden shophouses and traditional Chinese shops
items.note: The riverside quarter in town is easy to stroll, with photo spots and small souvenir shops along the way.

items.activity: Pay respects to Luang Pho Sothon at Wat Sothon Wararam Worawihan
items.note: Open Monday–Friday 6:30 AM–4:30 PM, Saturday–Sunday 6:30 AM–5:00 PM. The temple sits on the Bang Pakong River and holds the province's most revered Buddha image. Dress modestly.

items.activity: Dinner at a riverside restaurant in town, then back to the hotel
items.note: Paet Riu has several restaurants along the Bang Pakong. Pick a seat with a sunset view over the water.

blocks.html: Day one is deliberately light on walking, focused on lingering over coffee, with the old town saved for late afternoon when the sun softens. If you take your coffee seriously, you can add Good Barista & Coffee Beans — the owner is a Q grader who selects the beans personally, and the shop is minimal in warm brown tones.

blocks.text: Day 2 — 100-year-old Ban Mai Market in the morning

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Catch the century-old market before the crowds, then head home

items.activity: Check out, then head to the 100-year-old Ban Mai Market
items.note: A century-old wooden market on the Bang Pakong River, open Saturday–Sunday 8:00 AM–5:00 PM. Come early and it's easier to walk, with the stalls still fully stocked.

items.activity: Eat your way through the market — sweets, savory bites, dried goods
items.note: The food is cheap, and there's an old-style coffee shop, Pae Oei, that still keeps its original feel — sip a coffee while looking out over the old wooden houses.

items.activity: Follow up with a riverside cafe near the market, like 9 Ma Café
items.note: The shop sits just before you reach Ban Mai Market, with an outdoor zone right on the Bang Pakong River. Relaxed vibe, drinks start around 60–100 THB.

items.activity: Lunch to close out the trip, then head home
items.note: Pick a restaurant along the way or back in town before getting on the road to Bangkok.

blocks.title: About parking
blocks.html: Ban Mai Market has a private parking lot across the street — just walk across and you're there. Parking runs about 30–40 THB. It gets crowded on weekends, so arriving before 9 AM makes finding a spot easier.

blocks.text: The Bang Pakong riverside cafes we picked

items.name: Nava House Cafe
items.blurb: A riverside cafe on the grounds of Pukae Riverside. There's an air-conditioned room with seats right on the river, so you don't have to sweat it out, or you can take the shaded outdoor zone under the trees when the weather's nice.

items.name: Tang Seng Chua Saen Phudat
items.blurb: The big new branch of Tang Seng Chua, a mooncake-pastry brand with over 90 years of history. The Korean-palace-style building has become a photo landmark, with a cafe, pastries, and a souvenir zone all in one place.

items.name: 9 Ma Café
items.blurb: Sits just before Ban Mai Market, with an outdoor zone right on the Bang Pakong River. Relaxed vibe and good food and desserts — a nice stop right after the morning market.

items.name: Good Barista & Coffee Beans
items.blurb: A shop for serious coffee people — the owner is a Q grader who selects the beans personally. Minimal decor in warm brown tones, with photo corners and quiet seats to sip your coffee.

items.name: Woody Haus Café
items.blurb: A Korean-style cafe with a clean, easy-on-the-eyes tone. There's a soft-lit indoor zone and a stylish outdoor corner, plus a range of bakery items. Great for photos.

items.name: Chan Mak
items.blurb: A contemporary Thai-style riverside cafe with a leafy, shaded setting. The simple design suits a slow, unhurried break by the water.

blocks.html: The prices listed are rough ranges per drink and may shift depending on the menu and the time. We chose places with consistent reviews that were still open at the time of writing, but check each shop's page before you set out for their weekly closing day.

blocks.text: Making the most of Paet Riu old town

items: Wat Sothon Wararam Worawihan — pay respects to Luang Pho Sothon, the province's most revered Buddha image, on the Bang Pakong River. Open daily from early morning. Dress modestly.
Riverside old-town quarter — wooden shophouses and traditional Chinese shops, good for photos and picking up small souvenirs.
100-year-old Ban Mai Market — a century-old wooden riverside market, open Saturday–Sunday, with plenty of food, an old-style coffee shop, and folk performances.

blocks.title: Planning a weekday trip
blocks.html: If you come on a weekday when Ban Mai Market is closed, swap it for more old-town walking and in-town cafe-hopping — places like Woody Haus or Good Barista — and save the market for next time.

blocks.text: Getting there and where to stay

blocks.html: Driving from Bangkok to Paet Riu is easiest — take the motorway or the Bang Na–Trat road, about 1–1.5 hours. If you're not driving, take the Eastern Line train to Chachoengsao station and connect with local transport in town. The town isn't big; the cafes and old town are close together. Ban Mai Market and a few of the riverside cafes sit slightly outside town, so having your own car makes things smoother.
Staying in town makes everything easier — the cafes, old town, and temple are all a short drive apart. If you want to compare hotel prices and locations, see the summary on our accommodation roundup.

faq.q: What days is the 100-year-old Ban Mai Market open?
faq.a: Only Saturday–Sunday and public holidays, 8:00 AM–5:00 PM. If you want to catch the market, plan your trip across a Saturday or Sunday. Coming in the morning makes for easier walking with the stalls still fully stocked.

faq.q: Which Bang Pakong riverside cafe is the most comfortable to sit at?
faq.a: Nava House Cafe has an air-conditioned room with seats right on the river, ideal on hot days. 9 Ma Café and Chan Mak stand out for their open-air riverside zones, best for sitting in the morning or evening when the sun is softer.

faq.q: How many days are right for a cafe trip in Paet Riu?
faq.a: Two days and one night is about perfect. Day one is cafe-hopping with an old-town walk and a visit to Luang Pho Sothon; day two catches Ban Mai Market in the morning before heading home. You can do it in a single day, but it'll feel a bit rushed.

faq.q: Can I visit Paet Riu without my own car?
faq.a: Yes. Take the Eastern Line train to Chachoengsao station and connect with local transport in town. The cafes and old town are close enough to walk or grab a ride. But Ban Mai Market and a few riverside cafes are outside town, so having your own car is more convenient.
